Living Scaffold has less 3D occlusion and viewpoint control, but its L2 task introduces a second articulated body whose support and future moves depend on the first. The comparison supports Living Scaffold being above this low visual-control anchor on state-dependent planning while remaining a different capability mix.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 Constellation task uses cursor-conditioned particle convergence, two decoy basins, noise stars, and a single coordinate-tolerant click. It has an active visual search burden but no persistent articulated-body state after the click. Living Scaffold L2 requires a sequence of body selections and one-cell actions with gravity and support changes. These are comparable broad rungs with different burdens: Constellation is stronger on active cursor observation, while Living is stronger on dependent planning.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board requires continuous tilt-driven motion through three ordered lamps while avoiding three walls and three wells, with acceleration, friction, bounce, and collision outcomes replayed by the grader. Living Scaffold L2 uses synchronous cardinal one-cell actions and no continuous momentum; its challenge is discrete body-support planning. The Gyroscopic task therefore supplies a materially stronger precision/control burden and is a reasonable harder reference for Living L2.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 courier traverses five face gates in an 18x11 warehouse while the die orientation is hidden except at four scanners; gate acceptance depends on the rolled top face and the route must cross every gate in order. Living Scaffold L2 exposes all body, fruit, exit, and rock geometry and has no hidden orientation memory. The courier is a substantially harder memory and route-state reference; the generator's 48-105-roll bounds are not used here as proof of difficulty.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 candy task requires four valid adjacent swaps on a changing 5x5 board, deterministic gravity/refill cascades, an exact target score, and avoiding terminal black-licorice contact. Each accepted swap changes the later decision state. Living Scaffold L5 has a smaller discrete articulated-body state with visible geometry, so the current Living L2 is well below this sustained changing-board planning reference.

visible_baseline_solution.description: A normal screenshot-only solver sees the 10x8 garden, rock ledges, colored articulated bodies, yellow fruit, and color-matched flower exits. It must select a live body, move its head one cardinal cell at a time, and inspect the resulting screenshot after each action. Moving onto fruit grows that body; other moves shift its tail. After every move unsupported bodies fall together, so the solver must preserve a transitive support chain and choose an order that does not drop a body. Once all fruit is eaten, a body whose head reaches its matching exit disappears; support can then change again. Undo can restore the last successful state and Restart can recover from a bad plan. The solver submits only after the replayed state has no dead flag, no remaining food, and no remaining bodies.
visible_baseline_solution.baseline_fit: This L2/full problem is materially more state-dependent than the one-click approved Cursor-Controlled Constellation Hunt L2, but lacks the continuous precision of Gyroscopic Tilt Board L3 and the hidden orientation or changing-board burdens of Blind Dice Courier L4 and Exact-Change Candy Cascade L5.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current L2/full label fits the implemented structural burden. Compared with L1 Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine, Living Scaffold has less 3D raycast perception but adds a dependent second-body support problem. Compared with L2 Cursor-Controlled Constellation Hunt, it requires a longer stateful plan rather than one active-vision click. It remains below L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board because movement is synchronous one-cell control without momentum or continuous correction, and it is below L4 Blind Dice Courier and L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade because the relevant geometry and state are visible and the task has fewer coupled stages. The source supports keeping the baseline as a provisional numeric assignment, not as empirical calibration.

The default task has no control_condition, so the generator falls back to PROFILES[2]; the explicit condition supplies the same profile, full mode, and live run identity. The explicit form adds control_condition metadata, and a separate materializer could change task identity, but the source generator's board identity and physics are otherwise the same.

findings.claim: The source supports active structural differences among the five profiles but does not establish uniform numeric difficulty across generated seeds.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator retries until physics.solve returns any path and then certifies the replay; it does not constrain solution length, branching, number of critical choices, or human/agent success. The task metadata also records human usability and difficulty calibration as pending.

evidence.explanation: Generation samples limited rock/target layouts and accepts the first solvable candidate without a difficulty witness beyond solvability.

findings.recommended_action: Keep the source-supported labels provisionally and calibrate multi-seed human and computer-use-agent performance before treating the numeric levels as measured difficulty.

findings.claim: The 3->4 pair is clearly distinguishable but is not a pure monotonic increase.
findings.causal_explanation: L4 adds a third coupled body, fruit, and exit, which increases support dependencies, but it simultaneously disables return_blossom and moves the second exit back to the far-bank range. The source does not quantify which effect dominates on every generated layout.

findings.recommended_action: Retain the provisional ordering for now; compare seed-level decision depth and human/agent performance, then revise the pair only if the added body does not dominate the easier-side exit change.

concise_summary: Keep Living Scaffold at L2/full and retain the five structural profiles provisionally. The source shows active state-dependent support changes, a visible screenshot-solvable board, and equivalent full/simplified physics with mode-bound grading. Absolute calibration and historical pre-controls preservation remain unproven.
limitations: This report uses source analysis only; no browser, benchmark evaluation, multi-seed generation run, human calibration, or computer-use-agent measurement was performed.
The approved anchors span different capability mixes, so their levels provide concrete comparisons rather than a single scalar difficulty metric.
The generator certifies solvability but does not provide a per-seed difficulty guarantee.
No historical pre-controls implementation or fixed-seed output is available in the supplied source.
